daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

President Prabowo summoned the TNI Commander and Minister of Higher Education to Hambalang to discuss indigenous Dayak communities and forest fires. The meeting signals continued presidential attention to Kalimantan's environmental and social challenges. This comes as BNPB reports that thousands of fire hotspots in Kalimantan continue to increase.

  • Nahdlatul Ulama's 35th Muktamar approved a new mechanism for selecting the PBNU chairman, with the decision made through closed voting to determine whether the next chairman will be chosen by AHWA appointment rather than direct election.
  • The Muktamar also decided that Rais Aam and PBNU chairman will be prohibited from holding concurrent positions.
  • BNPB stated that a Constitutional Court ruling (261/2025) has made it easier for the government to designate national or regional disaster status.
  • The DPR will host the Inter-Parliamentary Speakers' Conference in 2027.
  • A draft asset forfeiture bill is being prepared that will cover not only corruption but also 12 other criminal offences including tax crimes and human trafficking.
  • The Attorney General's Office reminded former BGN deputy Lodewyk Pusung that pretrial motions are limited to once, as he filed his third challenge regarding asset seizures.
  • Options for implementing the State Policy Guidelines (PPHN) are being discussed, with choices between amending the 1945 Constitution or issuing an MPR decree.

Foreign Policy & Defence

The Indonesian Foreign Ministry has not received reports of Indonesian citizens affected by the flash floods in Nepal and Tibet, which have killed 633 people and left nearly 3,000 missing. BNPB announced that Japan is preparing three helicopters to assist Indonesia's forest fire suppression efforts. Indonesia also discussed bilateral cooperation with New Zealand on food security and renewable energy.

  • The Indonesian Embassy in Tokyo held a consultation forum to improve services for Indonesian citizens in Japan.
  • The Indonesian Embassy in Seoul is working to encourage 50,000 Muslim diaspora members to become drivers of the Islamic economy.
  • Indonesia needs to leverage BRICS and OECD membership to boost national competitiveness, according to analysts.

Other

The NTT earthquake death toll stands at 111, with 8,794 aftershocks recorded and 89,618 houses damaged, BNPB reported. The emergency response period has been extended until 12 September. Ministers have pledged to rebuild public facilities and expedite transport infrastructure repairs in the affected areas.

  • The modus operandi of 40 steel companies evading taxes has been revealed by authorities.
  • The Indonesia Stock Exchange reported that seven companies are in the pipeline for IPOs, with four from the healthcare sector.
  • Indonesia is pushing to improve the investment climate and remove bottlenecks to attract more foreign capital.
  • BNPB deployed a water-bombing helicopter to fight forest fires in West Papua.
  • Indonesia is targeting a US$521 billion sports industry to boost economic growth, officials announced.
